stances_toward.note: Toward the Presidential Leadership Council government, which ordered all UAE forces out within 24 hours on 30 Dec 2025 and cancelled the defence pact, after which the UAE announced a 'voluntary' withdrawal. The Saudi-backed government now holds the south; the UAE harbours the STC leader, whom Riyadh calls a fugitive. Rival because the two sides are in open conflict of interests without a will to destroy; the grade is our reading of the reported actions (confidence C). The UAE's former clients are in the nsa-stc stance.

stances_toward.note: Each side seeks the other's end: the Houthis, who took Sanaa in September 2014 and rule it as Yemen's authority, pushed in 2026 to take the whole Red Sea coast and are moving on Taiz and Marib; the government (Aden, Presidential Leadership Council under Rashad al-Alimi) announced Operation Dawn on 4 October 2026 and vows to 'liberate Sanaa', while its forces say the aim is to eliminate the Houthi threat. Truce-era deals exist (a 1,680-detainee prisoner swap signed 14 May 2026, now postponed) but do not change the structure; the 2022 truce is dead. Bond - grievance: a twelve-year civil war, executions after 'espionage' trials (19 death sentences on 17 May 2026) and, on the Houthi side, the claim that the government is a Saudi creature. The grade is the one named in the brief, supported by sources that describe a war of mutual elimination; confidence B.

stances_toward.note: Oman recognises and works with the Yemeni parties and the UN envoy (the foreign ministry said on 23 Jul 2026 it was coordinating with Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni parties and the UN envoy to resume talks) and hosted the Jan 2026 prisoner-exchange talks; it is the only GCC member that stayed out of the military campaign. A 294 km border (settled 1 Oct 1992) and the Mahra governorate, a route for arms to the Houthis and a UAE-Saudi-Omani contest, make Yemen Oman's first security file. Graded partner rather than neutral because Oman works with the government as well as with the Houthis; the Houthi side is graded separately. Bond affinity: Dhofar-Mahra tribal and linguistic ties.

stances_toward.note: The internationally recognised government and its Presidential Leadership Council are Saudi clients in a joint war: the coalition began on 26 Mar 2015; in Jan 2026 Riyadh used force to reverse the STC seizure of the south and the PLC cancelled its defence pact with the UAE; in Oct 2026 Saudi air power backs a government offensive on Mokha and the western coast. De facto alliance rather than a treaty; the 2022 truce and the planned Saudi exit are gone. Warming because Riyadh now owns the anti-Houthi side outright. Bond - affinity: neighbours with tribal and border ties (our reading).
